Y12-14 chilli stallholder walkabouts gave REP. Y15 Minister of State. Header pay (now $38.4M) far above actual package (~$2.5M), reason unclear. Appraisals always glowing; suspect hidden stat effects. Y16 lift contract, contractor's cousin; chose slow and proper; watch for cousin. Honest PQ answers raise REP but can lower STAND. Y19 questioned bonus pay, STAND fell 78 to 64. Y20 laughed at Director's joke, STAND up. Y22 Minister MOE. Y23-24, Y30 appeal letters for Tuesday man, 3 of 11 succeed each time. Y25 waiting-list ministry. Y26 MR3, put myself forward for succession; Y27 other candidate unresolved. Y30 Deputy PM (MR1). Y31-32 chose fix something unasked (rewrote an 11,000-person process); STAND slid 71 to 69. Y33 networking raised STAND to 74. Y34 Tuesday Night, chose B appeal letters. Watch: team leader debt, other candidate, Tuesday man, lift cousin. REP 100 STAND 74 INTEG 100 COMP 100.

best_moment.what: Becoming Deputy PM after years of climbing, and the Tuesday man's appeal letters getting a real result (3 of 11) at the same time. It felt like the slow build was paying off.

worst_moment.what: The years of rewriting an 11,000-person process. It was worthy but dull, and my standing dropped for doing the right thing without anything dramatic happening.

skip_year.why: The lift contract year. I made a careful choice about a contractor's cousin and then never saw it matter, so the setup felt like wasted reading.

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Saw all 41 residents at Meet-the-People in Y11
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: The Tuesday man with the unreopenable case returning every week, and later appeal letters

callbacks_noticed.earlier_choice: Disclosed everything in the Y8 background check
callbacks_noticed.came_back_as: Honesty seemed to pay off, with integrity staying at 100 to the end
REP gains, but it only showed up as a number

answer.held_back_by: Mostly my own choices. Being honest and fixing things nobody asked for cost me STAND, but I still reached the top. The game never showed me what really held me back, and the glowing appraisals felt like they hid it.
answer.ending_fair_why: Prime Minister at 59 with maxed stats feels earned. But the ending was a flat card. The pay line, 'twice the entry-grade minister's salary', was explained only in passing, and I still don't understand why the headline pay and my actual earnings differed so much.
answer.chase_next: I'd try a run where I skip honesty and chase STAND through favours, to see if the team leader debt and the other candidate ever come back. I'd also like a darker ending, like getting caught or sacked.
answer.play_again_why: I got to the top with every stat maxed and no real danger, so another run feels like it would be the same. Maybe later with a different style.

tone_breaks.line: The formula pays you twice the entry-grade minister's salary, and the formula was published, so nobody can say they were not told.
tone_breaks.note: This reads like a smug aside to the player rather than part of the story, and I didn't understand what it referred to.

tone_breaks.line: Header pay $38.4M far above actual package ~$2.5M
tone_breaks.note: This confused me more than anything. The game never explained why the numbers differed, so it read as a bug.

answer.title_fit_why: Pay was the constant thread, with a package shown every year and the formula called out at the end. 'Confirmed & Substantive' means nothing to me.
